blocks.inputs: Validated account and form fields; current stored enabled flag and alternative identity.
blocks.invariants: A disabled account cannot authenticate; re-enable cannot restore an old login identifier; existing database row IDs are preserved.
blocks.outputs: Updated availability or authenticated enabled account, never credential bytes in responses.
blocks.pseudocode: Validate request; load account; reject disabled or invalid; on true-to-false rotate identity; commit flag plus identity; reload state on later requests.
blocks.scale_or_limits: One account lookup per protected request; bounded teaching application with no new capacity guarantee.

mappings.null_or_default: Existing rows become enabled; new rows default true
mappings.source: Existing user row without enabled column
mappings.transformation: Add column with true default without drop/reseed
mappings.validation: Inspect table columns and preserve row identity

mappings.null_or_default: Missing or invalid fields are rejected
mappings.transformation: On disable rotate login identity once
mappings.validation: CSRF and authenticated enabled-manager checks precede mutation

blocks.classification: Reject invalid/unauthorized requests; treat migration errors as failures rather than default success.
blocks.handling: Validate before mutation, retain existing account data and report actionable errors without sensitive values.
blocks.observable_result: Rejected request does not change stored state; failed initialization does not drop rows.
blocks.recovery: Correct the input or isolated configuration, rerun the exact failed request and regression.
blocks.trigger: An invalid login, forged/disabled session, missing CSRF or schema initialization error.

blocks.consistency_or_atomicity: Account availability and session identifier rotate within one transaction; source effects remain recorded by IMP.
blocks.failure_handling: Keep failed evidence and source state; never claim VFY success from an IMP syntax check.
blocks.idempotency: Same completed operation is not repeated; migration and repeated disable do not re-seed or resurrect data.
blocks.order_and_condition: Read the exact predecessor result and precondition every source write; tests use fresh database state.
blocks.resource_or_effect: Declared application resource and its isolated test database

steps.expected_result: Current application code handles enabled status, session revocation and legacy data without broadening access.
steps.failure_boundary: Any failed precondition, source check or test leaves a visible incomplete work item.
logic: Read the exact current baseline and declared design.
Apply only the preconditioned implementation files.
Execute the declared local checks, retaining actual output and immutable final source.
steps.purpose: Implement account availability, protected admin editing, revocation and additive SQLite migration.
steps.transaction_boundary: One bounded source implementation work item; request-time data transactions follow the approved design.
